minutes.headline: Select Board repealed policy 2.13 and waived first refusal on two Kilburn Street lots amid heated public comment.
minutes.summary: Board and public comment ran long on staff morale, vacancies and criticism of the vice chair. The board waived first refusal on two Chapter 61B lots, amended a motor vehicle license, and repealed the public communications policy. The interim town manager gave his first report, including the police chief's retirement, and the board discussed ARPA fund prioritization.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to repeal policy 2.13, the public communications policy.
The board voted unanimously of members present to waive the town's right of first refusal on two lots at 20 Kilburn Street, which are in Chapter 61B.
The board amended an auto dealer license to wholesale and brokering only, with changed business hours, on a voice vote.
The interim town manager gave his first report, and the board discussed ARPA funding; requests exceed the remaining balance and no allocations were voted.
Public comment ran long, with criticism of the vice chair, concern about the cost of a town manager search firm, and a firefighters union statement on low morale.

why_it_matters: Repealing policy 2.13 changes the rules the board follows for public communications, which affects how residents and officials deal with each other at meetings and in public.
Waiving first refusal on the Kilburn Street lots means the town will not buy that land, and the written promise that the rest stays in Chapter 61B was still to be supplied.
ARPA requests exceed what is left, so a decision on which requests are funded is still pending, and the town manager search cost is a budget item residents objected to.
watch_next: The board's ARPA rankings, collated by a member and handed out at the meeting, which are the next step toward allocating the remaining funds.
The outdoor dining policy, targeted for a September meeting.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on all three non-procedural votes, and the accounts payable warrant amounts and the outdoor dining target are the same in both. They differ on the town manager search firm cost ($155,000 against $15,000), on the reserve fund transfer and ARPA figures that appear only in our minutes, and on the attendee list.
